translation_notes: URIRef("http://test") -> <http://test>, URIRef("http://example.org/count") -> <http://example.org/count>, Literal("not-a-number", datatype=XSD.integer) -> "not-a-number"^^xsd:integer, all three as term islands INSIDE the existing np.assertion.add((...)) tuple: the statement structure is byte-for-byte the same

FINDING: the mechanical draft used np.assertion += g{ ... }; that cannot work here because Nanopub.assertion is a read-only property (no setter) - an augmented assignment rebinds the attribute, whereas the original .add() only mutates the object. Same class of friction as the PySOSA example (module global there, read-only property here): the g{} island is fine, the += that usually carries it is not always available.
term islands in an argument tuple work verbatim, including the multi-line parenthesised layout and the trailing comma

context shim nanopub_context.py: puts the corpus checkout of nanopub-py on sys.path (the package is not installed but all its runtime deps are) and carries _minimal_valid_nanopub, a helper defined a few lines above the region in the same test module and thus having no import line; copied verbatim from tests/test_nanopub.py:763-773. Imported identically by both sides.
driver: the region is its own oracle - pytest.raises(MalformedNanopubError, match="not-a-number") only succeeds if the literal really carries xsd:integer; self is unused so the fixture passes None
negative control run: writing ^^xsd:string instead of ^^xsd:integer makes the driver fail with DID NOT RAISE
